column1: # Host-to-peer readings for examples/dual-plane.dc, in the shape a monitoring
# script writes them: a timestamp, the host, the peer it measured against,
# and a column per metric. The third column is headed `peer`, so it names
# each row's far end, and every metric after it is a flow from host to peer.
#   R01 <-> R03   every server in rack R01 sends 20 Gb/s (then 18) to its
#                 namesake in R03, in the other pod, and gets 3 Gb/s back.
#                 Both ends report it: R01's rows say uplink 20, downlink 3,
#                 and R03's say uplink 3, downlink 20 -- so uplink/s and
#                 downlink/s put the same traffic on the cables, the right
#                 way round (downlink runs from the peer to the host).
#   R01/s5        its round trips to R03/s5 take 48 us where the others take
#                 about 12, and it retransmits: averaged on the cables, rtt
#                 shows where that pair's traffic ran.
# Tick a metric, then "load the cables" on its card. uplink/s and
# downlink/s add up on each cable; rtt is in us, which does not add up
# along a path, so each cable shows the average of the flows across it.
# "values on the cables" in the Cable load panel prints each cable's figure.
